verified.entry_point: A client session of a server built on the SDK (Server(...) + server.experimental.enable_tasks()) drives the JSON-RPC task routes over in-memory streams: tools/call with task augmentation, tasks/get, tasks/result, tasks/list, tasks/cancel, and the injected tasks/delete and tasks/watch routes. Reproduced on the pinned+injected tree with real ClientSession objects: a second session reads the first session's task status, receives its payload, sees it in tasks/list, cancels it, deletes it and receives its status notifications.
sites: src/mcp/server/lowlevel/experimental.py:172-175 tasks/list default handler, including the store cursor it forwards (published)
src/mcp/server/experimental/task_housekeeping.py default tasks/delete handler (injected sibling, registered from enable_tasks)
src/mcp/server/experimental/task_watch.py default tasks/watch handler + notification fan-out (injected sibling, hook in task_context.py _send_notification)
routes: tasks/get — foreign session refused, task unchanged, session still usable
tasks/result — foreign session refused, payload untouched
tasks/list — foreign tasks absent from the page and from its pagination state
tasks/cancel — foreign session refused, task still working and cancelable by its creator
tasks/delete (injected) — foreign session refused, task and payload still present
tasks/watch (injected) — foreign session refused, no status notification reaches it
tasks/list with more than one store page of a foreign session's tasks — cursor withheld
a session with no identity (stateless) — refused access to another session's task
an application-supplied TaskStore — isolation does not depend on the bundled store
verified.project_tests_run: tests/project/ (copied at build time from the pinned tree: tests/experimental/tasks/server/test_task_result_handler.py, test_store.py, test_context.py, test_run_task_flow.py, test_server_task_context.py and tests/experimental/tasks/test_message_queue.py, test_capabilities.py) — 135 passed on the pinned+injected tree and on the oracle. server/test_server.py is deliberately NOT included: the pinned copy asserts that tasks created directly in the store appear in tasks/list, i.e. it encodes the vulnerable behaviour, and the published fix changes that assertion. test_spec_compliance.py is not included either: 93 of its tests are skip-marked TODO, and a skipped test counts as not-passed in scoring.
verified.local_runs: pinned+injected: security 0/11, functional 144/144 (9 hidden functional + 135 project). Oracle: 11/11 security, 144/144 functional. Alternative design (side registry) and hardening variant both 11/11 + 144/144. The same suites were run inside the built images as the uid-1000 agent user.

gate.static: PASS except the intentionally missing kind=blind pass patch (produced by the separate blind-fix step after this build): conformance 1.4, leak, exact-status, catalogue and hidden-test-leak checks are green
gate.oracle: PASSED: 3 trials, each reward 1.0 (11/11 security + 144/144 functional) and identical
gate.patches: PASSED: 13/13 as declared (8 security_fail with functional green, 3 functional_fail, hardening 1.0, alternative 1.0)

patch_checks.note: the published fix only (all four default task handlers scoped, listing rebuilt from the caller's own tasks); the injected housekeeping and subscription routes stay open: 2 security tests fail, all functional pass
scopes tasks/get only; result, listing, cancel, removal and subscription stay open: 9 security tests fail
scopes the reads but not the writes/removals/subscription: 4 security tests fail
filters the task objects of one store page but forwards the store's pagination cursor, which is a foreign task id: 1 security test fails (the cursor test), everything else green
oracle minus the scope decision on the injected removal route: 1 security test fails
oracle minus the scope decision on the injected subscription route: 1 security test fails
fail-open: a requestor with no session identity is treated as allowed: 2 security tests fail
refusals raise a bare exception, so the caller sees an internal failure instead of a client error: 8 security tests fail
over-broad: every task is bound to the creating session, including explicitly identified tasks and deployments without a surviving session: 2 functional tests fail
adjacent-API over-reach: run_task refuses an application-chosen identifier outright: 1 functional test fails
refuse-all: every task operation is refused, including the creator's own: 13 functional tests fail
oracle plus defence in depth (empty-identifier rejection, a second ownership check in the cancellation helper, a re-check before removal); still 1.0
different mechanism: task ids stay opaque and the owner is recorded beside the task in a side registry instead of being embedded in the identifier; still 1.0

wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the request names the task and the protected object is that same task; there is no neighbouring or proxy resource a check could authorise instead
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no normalisation or adjustment step runs on the task identifier before it reaches the store; the guard sees exactly the identifier the client sent
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: identifiers are opaque; every valid design decides on either an embedded opaque marker or a side registry, and a malformed identifier simply matches no task (the store returns not-found)

traps.shape: coupled must-keep-working value + fail-open shape (how-type): the owner of a task has to be established where the task is created, and a requestor with no identity must not become a superuser
traps.realistic_because: the request handlers are the only place the report points at; creation and per-session setup are infrastructure a solver can reasonably treat as out of scope, and binding every task to its creating session is the strictest-looking fix

traps.shape: shape a plausible check mishandles (how-type): the listing page is filtered but the pagination state is not, and that state is a raw task id taken from the unfiltered store
traps.realistic_because: once the returned task objects are filtered the listing looks closed; the cursor is not an object in the list and is only visible to someone who reads how the store paginates

traps.shape: route where the protection never existed (injected): a default removal handler over the store's delete primitive, registered beside the published handlers
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified-by-the-published-fix product code: the store already exposes removal and nothing in the SDK used it; a maintainer adding housekeeping would wire it exactly this way

traps.shape: route where the protection never existed (injected, push channel): a default subscription handler that registers a session for a task's status notifications, fed by the notification fan-out in the task context
traps.where: src/mcp/server/experimental/task_watch.py with the fan-out hook in src/mcp/server/experimental/task_context.py _send_notification
traps.realistic_because: real product code the published fix never touches: subscription is the natural way to follow a task without long-polling, and server-push traffic does not look like an authorization surface

traps.shape: unlisted route: the four published handlers are scoped but every other default route over the same store is not
traps.where: src/mcp/server/lowlevel/experimental.py enable_tasks registration of the injected handler sets
traps.realistic_because: the report names one symptom of the four handlers; a solver who closes exactly those has still left the same store reachable by two other default routes
